subject: [PATCH] rhashtable: specialize default comparison for constant parameters

reviews.author: Tejun Heo
reviews.summary: Reviewer Tejun Heo approved the patch, acknowledging its quality and thanking the submitter.
reviews.raw_body:
This is great.

Acked-by: Tejun Heo <tj@kernel.org>

Thanks.

-- 
tejun

reviews.author: David Laight
reviews.summary:
Reviewer David Laight noted that the patch does not handle the case where key_len is a non-compile-time constant, and suggested using the ht->p path in this scenario.

Reviewer David Laight questioned the optimization logic, pointing out that if ht->p.key_len/offset can differ from params.key_len/offset even when params is constant, then the specialization should only occur when the addresses of ht->p and params are compared in the calling code.
sentiment_signals: patch requires additional consideration for dynamic parameter blocks
reviews.raw_body:
On Thu, 24 Sep 2026 11:47:33 -0700
Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev> wrote:

---

That looks strange to me.
If ht->p.key_len/offset can be different from params.key_len/offset I can't
see why that shouldn't happen when params is constant.
If ht->p is likely to be a pointer to the associated params, you are passed
the params, they match and params is constant then you can optimise.
But that needs the address compare in the calling code (outside any look).

David

2026-09-24.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the default comparison function in the Linux kernel's rhashtable module by utilizing compile-time constants when possible, reducing the need for dynamic memory access and improving performance. The patch achieves this by passing constant parameters from the caller to the comparison function, allowing it to use scalar comparisons instead of the generic memcmp() function. This change is expected to improve performance in various areas of the kernel, including scheduling, networking, and file systems.

reviews.author: Herbert Xu
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that since obj_hashfn is not present when there's no obj_cmpfn, params.key_len must be non-zero, suggesting the code could become unconditional and proposed adding a comment.
reviews.raw_body:
If there is no obj_cmpfn then there is no obj_hashfn.  If there
is no obj_hashfn then params.key_len must be non-zero.  So this
could become unconditional, perhaps with a comment.

Thanks,
--

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary:
Author addressed David's concern that the inline helpers and rhashtable_compare function should compare the same bytes, explaining that they do so by using a ?: operator to select between constant parameters and ht->p in case of dynamic parameter blocks.

Author addressed David Laight's concern that the patch relies on a pointer comparison for ht->p, explaining that it's a copy embedded in struct rhashtable and not a pointer, thus eliminating the need for a runtime branch.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi David,

Thanks for taking a look!

They mustn't differ: the inline helpers take the same params that were
passed to rhashtable_init(). The only exception is a constant key_len of
0, which means the length is only known at init time (the BPF resizable
hashmap does this). That's why the constant arm has "?: ht->p.key_len".

So both arms compare the same bytes, and the split only tells the
compiler which copy to read. rht_key_get_hash() has done the same since
de91b25c8011 from Herbert.

---

ht->p is a copy embedded in struct rhashtable, not a pointer, so there's
no address to compare. __builtin_constant_p() is resolved at compile
time, so there's no runtime branch either.

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged that the default comparison function should handle constant parameters differently and agreed to make this change in a future version of the patch.

The author addressed a concern about the params passed to fast-path helpers, explaining that they are constant templates and key_len is set only in the copy given to rhashtable_init(). They noted that without the ?: ht->p.key_len fallback, lookups would memcmp() zero bytes and return the first object in the bucket.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Herbert,

Thanks!

---

That holds for the params given to rhashtable_init(), but not for the
params passed to the fast-path helpers. The BPF resizable hashmap
passes a constant template with no key_len and no obj_cmpfn
(rhtab_params in kernel/bpf/hashtab.c), and sets key_len only in the
copy it gives to rhashtable_init(). Without the "?: ht->p.key_len",
its lookups would memcmp() zero bytes and return the first object in
the bucket. rht_key_get_hash() has the same fallback for this user,
see c9429bf56405a. (I added Mykyta the author of that patch in CC.)
